is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses exclusively on Aedes aegypti and Aedes mascarensis (e.g. line 28-34: 'An example of this is Aedes aegypti... We explore a large whole-genome sequencing dataset of 729 Ae. aegypti across 15 countries').

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study examines mutations in Aedes aegypti resistance genes (e.g., Aedes vgsc mutations V410L, F1534C, V1016I/G, S989P, rdl A301S), not the specified Anopheles target markers.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No extractable genotype data for African Anopheles target markers is reported.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes sequenced are Aedes aegypti and Aedes mascarensis, not Anopheles.

is_primary_study.evidence: The paper re-analyses publicly available WGS datasets from NCBI SRA (lines 120-123: 'We searched the NCBI SRA database for "Aedes aegypti" sample data...').

sub_country_location.evidence: Mentions locations such as Rabai District in Kenya (lines 195-196, 382).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Samples come from varied public datasets across multiple years without bounded 3-year collection windows specified in the main text.

duplicate_risk.evidence: All genomic data were compiled from previously published NCBI SRA datasets (lines 120-123).

supplement.evidence: Supplementary files would not change eligibility since the study organism is Aedes aegypti.

assessment.summary: This study analyzes global genomic diversity in insecticide resistance genes (vgsc, rdl, ace-1, and GSTe2) across 729 Aedes aegypti and 7 Ae. mascarensis genomes sourced from public NCBI SRA records. Because it examines Aedes rather than Anopheles malaria vectors and relies on secondary data, it is not eligible.
exclusion_reasons: Paper does not study Anopheles mosquitoes (focuses on Aedes aegypti).
Does not genotype specified Anopheles target resistance markers.
Does not test African field populations of Anopheles.
Re-analysis of previously published public WGS data rather than primary data collection for Anopheles.
